specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:9:**Input**: User description: "P-RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing: Turn captured audio into text on the device, and photos into text through the backend, before saving the entry. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF02. Prototype states: 'Áudio — Processando / Transcrito / Erro' and 'Foto — Processando OCR / Reconhecido / Erro' (prototype extract, sections 2.3 and 4). On-device speech-to-text with whisper_ggml (audio never goes to the backend); OCR with POST /media/ocr; then POST /entries. Test material: docs/input/backend/fixtures/. Depends on: RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:15:- Q: RF01's own specification (FR-007) deliberately stopped at a plain, generic loading indicator for audio/photo recognition and explicitly deferred "a dedicated multi-state screen..., an editable review step..., or modality-specific retry affordances" to "a later unit." Does this unit replace that RF01 behavior, or sit alongside it? → A: This unit replaces RF01's placeholder recognition UX for the audio and photo tabs with the dedicated states the prototype defines (`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.3, §4): "Processando"/"Transcrevendo" (spinner, frozen waveform), "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" (editable text, explicit "Salvar"), and "Erro" (retry, plus photo's extra "Salvar só a foto"). Concretely, stopping a recording or supplying an image no longer completes the save automatically — it starts recognition, and the user reviews (and may edit) the result before explicitly confirming "Salvar." The text-entry tab (no recognition involved) is unaffected and stays exactly as RF01 built it. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where RF01's own text names this unit as the owner of that deferred behavior.)

specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:108:- The device is offline when OCR would normally be attempted: "Foto — Processando OCR" MUST resolve to "Foto — Erro" with a clear, offline-appropriate message (not a generic failure) rather than hanging; "Salvar só a foto" and "Tentar novamente" remain visible, but "Salvar" (from a would-be "Reconhecido" state) and "Salvar só a foto" both still require connectivity for the underlying `POST /entries` call, following the same offline-blocks-writes rule established in RF01.
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:111:- The app is backgrounded or killed while in "Processando"/"Transcrevendo", "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido", or "Erro": nothing is lost that mattered, because nothing was persisted yet. On return after a mere backgrounding, the state resumes normally (including any unsaved edits); after a process kill, the modal reopens to its default empty state and the user must recapture, the same lifecycle rule RF01 established for its own in-progress states, now extended to these additional ones.
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:120:- **FR-001**: When the user stops an audio recording (started in RF01's "Áudio" tab), the system MUST automatically begin on-device transcription and show "Áudio — Processando" — a spinner in place of the stop control, the waveform frozen and faded, the caption "Transcrevendo...", and the recorded duration — without creating any entry.
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:124:- **FR-005**: When the user supplies an image via the "Foto" tab (built in RF01), the system MUST automatically call the backend OCR endpoint (`POST /media/ocr`) and show "Foto — Processando OCR" — the photo thumbnail, a spinner, and the caption "Reconhecendo texto..." — without creating any entry.
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:130:- **FR-011**: If a capture is abandoned at any point while in "Processando"/"Transcrevendo", "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido", or "Erro" — the modal is closed, the user navigates away, or the user switches tabs — the system MUST NOT create any entry, and MUST discard any in-progress recognition, recognized/transcribed text, and edits held for that capture.
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:148:- **SC-006**: 0% of captures abandoned during "Processando"/"Transcrevendo", "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido", or "Erro" (for either modality) leave behind a persisted entry.

On-device speech-to-text with whisper_ggml (audio never goes to the backend); OCR with POST /media/ocr; then POST /entries. Test material: docs/input/backend/fixtures/. Depends on: RF01. specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:15:- Q: RF01's own specification (FR-007) deliberately stopped at a plain, generic loading indicator for audio/photo recognition and explicitly deferred "a dedicated multi-state screen..., an editable review step..., or modality-specific retry affordances" to "a later unit." Does this unit replace that RF01 behavior, or sit alongside it? → A: This unit replaces RF01's placeholder recognition UX for the audio and photo tabs with the dedicated states the prototype defines (`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.3, §4): "Processando"/"Transcrevendo" (spinner, frozen waveform), "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido" (editable text, explicit "Salvar"), and "Erro" (retry, plus photo's extra "Salvar só a foto"). Concretely, stopping a recording or supplying an image no longer completes the save automatically — it starts recognition, and the user reviews (and may edit) the result before explicitly confirming "Salvar." The text-entry tab (no recognition involved) is unaffected and stays exactly as RF01 built it. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I, where RF01's own text names this unit as the owner of that deferred behavior.)

specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:108:- The device is offline when OCR would normally be attempted: "Foto — Processando OCR" MUST resolve to "Foto — Erro" with a clear, offline-appropriate message (not a generic failure) rather than hanging; "Salvar só a foto" and "Tentar novamente" remain visible, but "Salvar" (from a would-be "Reconhecido" state) and "Salvar só a foto" both still require connectivity for the underlying `POST /entries` call, following the same offline-blocks-writes rule established in RF01.
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:111:- The app is backgrounded or killed while in "Processando"/"Transcrevendo", "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido", or "Erro": nothing is lost that mattered, because nothing was persisted yet. specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:124:- **FR-005**: When the user supplies an image via the "Foto" tab (built in RF01), the system MUST automatically call the backend OCR endpoint (`POST /media/ocr`) and show "Foto — Processando OCR" — the photo thumbnail, a spinner, and the caption "Reconhecendo texto..." — without creating any entry.
specs/004-stt-ocr-processing/spec.md:130:- **FR-011**: If a capture is abandoned at any point while in "Processando"/"Transcrevendo", "Transcrito"/"Reconhecido", or "Erro" — the modal is closed, the user navigates away, or the user switches tabs — the system MUST NOT create any entry, and MUST discard any in-progress recognition, recognized/transcribed text, and edits held for that capture.

| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |

### 2.4 Records
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |

### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |

All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.

|---|---|

| Tela 6 — Configurações — mais de 30 registros | "Sua evolução": 10-bar ochre chart + summary paragraph. |

| Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta | Centered dialog, red title "Apagar sua conta?", text on permanent, irreversible deletion; red button "Apagar tudo"; outline "Cancelar". |

4	/// The plain generic loading indicator every Save/recognition call in this
5	/// unit shows — no dedicated multi-state recognition screen (FR-007).
6	///
7	/// A fixed-length arc that only rotates (prototype-extract.md's "Continuous
8	/// spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state") rather
9	/// than Material's default indeterminate `CircularProgressIndicator`, whose
10	/// arc length itself pulses between near-zero and near-full — at the
11	/// near-zero point it reads as a short dash instead of a ring.
12	class CaptureLoadingIndicator extends StatefulWidget {
13	  const CaptureLoadingIndicator({super.key});
14	
15	  @override
16	  State<CaptureLoadingIndicator> createState() =>
17	      _CaptureLoadingIndicatorState();
18	}
19	
20	class _CaptureLoadingIndicatorState extends State<CaptureLoadingIndicator>
21	    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
22	  late final AnimationController _controller;
23	
24	  @override
25	  void initState() {
26	    super.initState();
27	    _controller = AnimationController(
28	      vsync: this,
29	      duration: const Duration(seconds: 1),
30	    )..repeat();
31	  }
32	
33	  @override
34	  void dispose() {
35	    _controller.dispose();
36	    super.dispose();
37	  }
38	
39	  @override
40	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
41	    return Center(
42	      child: SizedBox(
43	        width: DesignTokens.sizeLoadingIndicator,
44	        height: DesignTokens.sizeLoadingIndicator,
45	        child: RotationTransition(
46	          turns: _controller,
47	          child: const CircularProgressIndicator(
48	            strokeWidth: DesignTokens.strokeWidthLoadingIndicator,
49	            value: DesignTokens.valueLoadingIndicatorArc,
50	          ),
51	        ),
52	      ),
53	    );
54	  }
55	}

57	/// The prototype's actual "Erro" shape (prototype-extract.md §2.3,
58	/// research.md R4): a warning icon, the exact failure copy, an outline
59	/// "Tentar novamente" button, and — for Foto's "Salvar só a foto" only — an
60	/// optional secondary text action. Renders both Áudio's and Foto's "Erro"
61	/// states.
62	class RecognitionErrorView extends StatelessWidget {
63	  const RecognitionErrorView({
64	    required this.message,
65	    required this.onRetry,
66	    this.secondaryAction,
67	    super.key,
68	  });
69	
70	  final String message;
71	  final VoidCallback onRetry;
72	
73	  /// A `(label, onTap)` pair — used only by Foto's "Salvar só a foto"
74	  /// (US4); left `null` for Áudio.
75	  final (String, VoidCallback)? secondaryAction;
76	
77	  @override
78	  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
79	    final secondary = secondaryAction;
80	    return Column(
81	      mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
82	      children: [
83	        const Icon(
84	          Icons.error_outline,
85	          size: DesignTokens.sizeStatusIcon,
86	          color: DesignTokens.colorError,
87	        ),
88	        const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
89	        Text(
90	          message,
91	          textAlign: TextAlign.center,
92	          style: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorError),
93	        ),
94	        const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingMd),
95	        OutlinedButton(
96	          onPressed: onRetry,
97	          style: OutlinedButton.styleFrom(
98	            padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(
99	              horizontal: DesignTokens.spacingMd,
100	              vertical: DesignTokens.spacingSm,
101	            ),
102	          ),
103	          child: const Text('Tentar novamente'),
104	        ),
105	        if (secondary != null) ...[
106	          const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
107	          TextButton(onPressed: secondary.$2, child: Text(secondary.$1)),
108	        ],
109	      ],
110	    );
111	  }
112	}

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

aiTitle: Tela 4 export sheet status text styling

content.text:
All three fixes are in place and verified:

**Root cause** (all three symptoms traced to concrete code, not styling guesswork):

1. **(a) Fechar in Processando** — `export_processing_view.dart` used a bare `TextButton(child: const Text('Fechar'))`, which falls back to the app's global `textButtonTheme` (`colorPrimary`, `textLabelMd` — bold-ish sans at normal size). Pendente and Concluído, by contrast, explicitly override the style with `textMonoCaption` at 11px/secondary-gray. Processando was simply missing that override. Fixed by applying the same explicit style.

2. **(b) Status text weight** — Pendente/Processando used `DesignTokens.textTitleSm` (Karla **700**, 16px) for their status captions, while Concluído's "Resumo pronto" uses `textBodyMd` (Karla **400**, 14px). Switched both to `textBodyMd` to match.

3. **(c) Spinner vs. icon size** — this is why the earlier correction attempt didn't stick: the previous fix already sized the `SizedBox` to `sizeStatusIcon` (32×32), which *should* have matched the icon. The real culprit is Material's default `CircularProgressIndicator`, which is **indeterminate**: its arc length itself pulses between near-zero and near-full every animation cycle. Depending on the instant you look at it, it reads as a tiny dash or a thick near-complete ring — never a stable size matching the static check icon. I confirmed this by rendering the actual widget to a PNG (not guessing): the captured frame showed a barely-visible dot, not a 32px ring. This exact problem was already solved elsewhere in the codebase — `CaptureLoadingIndicator` (used for audio/photo recognition) replaces the default pulsing indicator with a fixed-75%-arc, thin-stroke, rotation-only spinner specifically to avoid this. I added an optional `size` parameter to that existing widget (default unchanged, so its other 5 call sites are unaffected) and reused it in `export_pending_view.dart` at `sizeStatusIcon`, instead of duplicating the fix.

**End-to-end confirmation**: rather than relying only on the existing unit tests (which don't cover these widgets' visual styling), I rendered all three states (Pendente, Processando, Concluído) to actual PNG screenshots via a throwaway golden-file test and visually compared them — confirming the Fechar links, status text weight, and spinner/icon size now read as one consistent system. `flutter analyze` and the full `export`/`capture` test suites (127 tests) pass with no regressions. All temporary test/screenshot files were removed afterward.
